mainTopic: Vows using the word חולין and רבי מאיר's view on inferring a positive from a negative; then linking a vow to שלמים meat after זריקת דמים
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about vows that use the word חולין (ordinary food). It says the first part follows רבי מאיר, who does not draw a positive conclusion from a negative statement. It then challenges the last part. In a משנה, רבי מאיר forbids 'לקרבן לא אוכל לך', because רבי אבא reads it as 'let it be a קרבן, so I won't eat it.' By the same reading, 'לחולין לא אוכל לך' should also be forbidden. The first answer is that the ברייתא's תנא agrees with רבי מאיר about inference but disagrees with him about the קרבן case. רב אשי answers instead that the wording differs: plain 'לחולין' is permitted, but 'לא לחולין' means 'like a קרבן' and is forbidden. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's list of טהור, טמא, נותר and פיגול. רמי בר חמא asks about someone who points to שלמים meat after זריקת דמים and says 'this is like that.' The question is whether he means the meat's original forbidden status or its current permitted status. רבא begins a proof from נותר and פיגול, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about vows using the word חולין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists different ways of using the word חולין in a vow. It rules which ones make the food forbidden and which leave it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If someone says 'חולין,' 'the חולין,' or 'like חולין,' whether he adds 'what I eat of yours' or 'what I don't eat of yours,' the food is permitted. If he says 'לחולין (not חולין) is what I eat of yours,' it is forbidden. If he says 'לחולין is what I won't eat of yours,' it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sorts out different vow wordings using the word חולין. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling food 'חולין' (ordinary) does not make it holy, so there is no vow. But 'לחולין' is read as 'לא חולין,' meaning 'not ordinary,' which means holy. So saying that about what he eats is a real vow. Saying it about what he does not eat leaves the food permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Ordinary, non-holy food
Read as 'לא חולין,' meaning not ordinary, so holy
Permitted
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: לחולין does not mean 'for חולין' here. It is read as 'לא חולין,' meaning 'not ordinary,' and that is why it can create a vow.

phrases.english: It was taught: 'Ordinary,' 'the ordinary,' 'like ordinary,'
whether 'that which I eat of yours'
or 'that which I do not eat of yours': permitted.
'Not ordinary is what I eat of yours': forbidden.
'Not ordinary is what I will not eat of yours': permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying חולין in any form is not a vow. Saying 'לחולין שאוכל לך' is a vow. Saying 'לחולין לא אוכל לך' is not a vow.

steps.title: The first part follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of the first part of the ברייתא as רבי מאיר. He does not infer a positive statement from a negative one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the author of the first part? It is רבי מאיר, who does not hold that from a negative you can infer a positive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the first part of the ברייתא follows, and answers that it is רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part, someone said 'What I do not eat of yours is חולין.' You might think this implies 'what I do eat is holy,' which would make it a vow. רבי מאיר does not draw that hidden positive from a negative statement, so the food stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
Who is the author?
The תנא whose opinion this is
From a negative statement you can infer the positive

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that רבי מאיר does not infer a positive from a negative, is the key that the next steps test against the end of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The first part, whose is it?
It is רבי מאיר,
who does not hold that from a negative
you can hear a positive.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the words 'שלא אוכל לך': not eating is ordinary, but that does not prove eating is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the first part of the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first part follows רבי מאיר, who does not infer a positive from a negative.

steps.title: Bringing in the קרבן case to test the last part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the last part of the ברייתא and cites a משנה where רבי מאיר forbids the food in a similar case with קרבן. That ruling had already seemed hard to fit with his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the last part: 'לחולין is what I won't eat of yours' is permitted. But we learned in a משנה: 'לקרבן is what I won't eat of yours,' and רבי מאיר forbids it. And that was difficult for us, since he does not infer a positive from a negative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the last part of the ברייתא. It reminds us of a parallel משנה, and of the difficulty we already had with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, 'לקרבן לא אוכל לך' seems to mean 'what I don't eat is not a קרבן,' and forbidding the food would require inferring 'so what I eat is a קרבן.' That is exactly the kind of inference רבי מאיר rejects. So his ruling there already needed an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Here it sounds like 'לא קרבן,' not an offering
Forbids
And this was difficult for us

phrases.english: Say the last part:
'Not ordinary is what I will not eat of yours': permitted.
But didn't we learn: 'Not an offering is what I will not eat of yours'?
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found later in this מסכתא, on דף יג.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר forbids.
And it was difficult for us:

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֵית לֵיהּ מִכְּלָל לָאו אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ הֵין?
phrases.english: But he does not hold that from a negative you hear a positive?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having placed the first part with רבי מאיר, the גמרא checks whether the last part also fits him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The last part of the ברייתא (לחולין לא אוכל לך is permitted)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel case with קרבן is forbidden by רבי מאיר, so the חולין case should be treated the same way. The challenge is completed in step 5.

steps.title: רבי אבא explains the קרבן case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that 'לקרבן לא אוכל לך' really means 'let it be a קרבן, therefore I won't eat it.' No hidden inference is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא said: It is as if he said, 'Let it be for a קרבן, and therefore I will not eat of yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אבא's earlier answer to the difficulty about רבי מאיר in the קרבן case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא reads לקרבן as 'לְקרבן,' meaning 'for an offering,' not 'לא קרבן.' The person directly declares the food a קרבן, and 'I won't eat' is just the result. So רבי מאיר forbids it without inferring a positive from a negative.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who answers the difficulty
It is as if he said
Let it be for an offering
Therefore

phrases.english: And רבי אבא said,
It is as if he said: Let it be for an offering,
therefore I will not eat of yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the old difficulty quoted in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לקרבן means 'not a קרבן,' so forbidding the food would need an inference from a negative.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words mean 'let it be a קרבן, so I won't eat,' which is a direct vow.

steps.title: The same reading should forbid the חולין case
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי אבא's reading, 'לחולין לא אוכל לך' should mean 'let it not be ordinary, so I won't eat it.' That is a vow, so why does the ברייתא permit it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, this is what he means: 'Let it not be ordinary, and therefore I will not eat of yours!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רבי אבא's reading to the last part of the ברייתא, which makes the challenge sharp. The ברייתא's ruling that the food is permitted now looks wrong according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לקרבן לא אוכל לך means 'it is a קרבן, so I won't eat,' then לחולין לא אוכל לך should mean 'it is not ordinary (it is holy), so I won't eat.' That is a direct vow, and no inference is needed. So the ברייתא should say אסור, not מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
This is what he is saying to him
Let it be

steps.whatToRemember: The first part of the ברייתא fits רבי מאיר. But רבי אבא's reading of the קרבן case suggests the last part (לחולין לא אוכל לך) should be forbidden, and the ברייתא says it is permitted. The next two steps give two different answers to this.

phrases.english: Here too, this is what he is saying to him:
Let it not be ordinary,
therefore I will not eat of yours!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי אבא's answer from step 4 and turns it against the last part of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The last part of the ברייתא, which permits 'לחולין לא אוכל לך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי אבא's reading, the words mean 'not ordinary, so I won't eat,' which is a direct vow even for רבי מאיר. So the food should be forbidden.

steps.title: The תנא agrees with רבי מאיר on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר in not inferring a positive from a negative. He disagrees with רבי מאיר about the case of קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא agrees with רבי מאיר on one point and disagrees with him on another. He agrees that you cannot learn a 'yes' from a 'no.' He disagrees about the case of קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. The ברייתא's author follows רבי מאיר only partly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא matches רבי מאיר's rule that a positive is not inferred from a negative. But this תנא does not accept רבי אבא's reading, 'let it be a קרבן, therefore I won't eat.' So in the same way, 'לחולין לא אוכל לך' does not mean 'let it not be חולין.' Without clear vow wording, the food stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The early sage who taught this ברייתא
In one point
Disagrees with him
From a 'no' you can hear a 'yes': inferring a positive from a negative

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the ברייתא rejects רבי מאיר completely. He agrees on the inference rule and disagrees only on how to read the קרבן wording.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: This תנא holds like רבי מאיר in one point
and disagrees with him in another?
He holds like him in one point:

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִכְּלָל לָאו אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ הֵין,
phrases.english: that he does not hold that from a 'no' you hear a 'yes,'
and he disagrees with him in another: about קרבן.
phrases.notes: He does not read 'לקרבן לא אוכל לך' the way רבי אבא did in Step 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the תנא's view: he partly agrees with רבי מאיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's author must fully follow רבי מאיר, including רבי אבא's reading of קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows רבי מאיר only on the inference rule, not on the קרבן reading, so 'לחולין' stays permitted

steps.title: רב אשי: the two cases use different wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the permitted case is 'לחולין,' and the forbidden case is 'לא לחולין,' which means 'not ordinary, but like a קרבן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this case is where he said 'as חולין,' and that case is where he said 'not as חולין.' That means: let it not be חולין, but like a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different answer. He says the wording in the two cases is not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's view, the ברייתא permits the food because the person said 'לחולין,' which only compares it to ordinary food. If he had said 'לא לחולין,' he would be clearly rejecting ordinary status, which means 'like a קרבן.' That would be a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: A later אמורא who offers a second answer
Ordinary, non-holy food
Which means / which implies

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
This is where he said 'as חולין,'
and that is where he said 'not as חולין,'
which means: let it not be חולין
but rather like a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר הָא דְאָמַר לַחוּלִּין וְהָא דְּאָמַר לָא לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 5, different from Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by their wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לחולין לא אוכל לך' should mean 'not חולין' and be forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'לא לחולין' means 'like a קרבן.' Plain 'לחולין' is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. The first: the תנא agrees with רבי מאיר only partly. The second, from רב אשי: the cases differ, 'לחולין' versus 'לא לחולין.'

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: pure, impure, נותר and פיגול make it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Comparing food to these kinds of offerings creates a vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. This sets up רמי בר חמא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that tying food to offerings with these labels makes it forbidden. This raises a question about an offering that is now permitted to eat, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an offering left over past its time to be eaten
An offering made with the intention to eat it after its proper time
Forbidden

phrases.english: 'Pure' and 'impure,' 'נותר' and 'פיגול': it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comparing food to these offerings makes it forbidden

steps.title: רמי בר חמא asks about שלמים meat after the blood is sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks what happens if someone vows that food is like שלמים meat after זריקת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: if someone says 'This is to me like the meat of שלמים after the sprinkling of the blood,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks a new question. What if the vow compares food to an offering whose meat is already permitted to eat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the blood is sprinkled, שלמים meat is forbidden. After it is sprinkled, the meat may be eaten. So it is unclear whether this comparison creates a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised an open question)
Peace-offerings, whose meat is eaten by the owners
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח
What is the law?

phrases.english: רמי בר חמא asked:
'This is upon me like the meat of peace-offerings
after the sprinkling of the blood': what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's rule about offerings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does comparing food to שלמים meat after זריקה create a vow?

steps.title: With those words, he is comparing it to something permitted
steps.stepSummary: If he actually said 'after the sprinkling,' he clearly compared the food to permitted meat, so there is no question.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said it with this wording, he is linking it to something permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question as it was asked. With these exact words, the answer is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'after the sprinkling of the blood,' the person himself pointed to the meat's permitted stage. So he made no vow, and the question must be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Wording, language
Something permitted
Links (ties) the food to something else to make it forbidden

phrases.english: If he said it with this wording,
he is linking it to something permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּקָאָמַר בְּהָדֵין לִישָּׁנָא בְּהֶיתֵּרָא קָא מַתְפֵּיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the question in Step 9 was framed
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of רמי בר חמא's question as worded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His explicit words name the permitted stage, so obviously no vow is made

steps.title: The real case: pointing and saying 'this is like that'
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he places שלמים meat next to permitted food and says 'this is like that.' Is he linking to the meat's original forbidden status or its current permitted status?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he puts down שלמים meat, puts permitted food next to it, and says 'this is like that.' What is the law? Is he linking to its original status, or to its permitted status?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא redefines רמי בר חמא's question. Now the person points at the meat without mentioning its stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat was once forbidden, before the blood was sprinkled, but now it is permitted. The question is which status his vow refers to. If it refers to the original status, the vow works. If it refers to the current status, it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Places, puts down
This is like that
In its original state

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question in vows: when a person links food to something, do we follow what that thing originally was or what it is now?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כְּגוֹן דְּמַחֵית בְּשַׂר זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים,
phrases.english: Rather: such as where he puts down meat of peace-offerings,
phrases.notes: This is meat after the blood was already sprinkled, so it is permitted now.

phrases.english: and puts permitted food next to it,
and says: 'this is like that,'
what is the law: is he linking to its original state,
phrases.notes: Its original state means before the blood was sprinkled, when the meat was still forbidden.

phrases.english: or is he linking to its permitted state?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן דְּמַחֵית בְּשַׂר זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reframes the question after the challenge in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When he says 'this is like that,' does the vow follow the meat's original forbidden status or its current permitted status?

steps.title: רבא points to נותר and פיגול in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a proof for רמי בר חמא's question from the משנה's ruling that comparing food to נותר or פיגול creates a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear a proof. The משנה lists נותר and פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to answer רמי בר חמא's question by pointing to a line in our משנה. This line sets up the proof; the גמרא explains how it works on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נותר and פיגול are meat from a קרבן. The משנה says that if someone compares food to them, the food becomes forbidden by a vow. רבא will use this case to show which status a person links to when he compares food to קרבן meat: the original status or the present one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear.' The phrase the גמרא uses to bring a proof from a source.
Meat of a קרבן that was left over past the time it may be eaten.
A קרבן that was brought with the intention of eating it after its proper time. It becomes forbidden.
The אמורא who brings the proof here.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
Notar and piggul.
phrases.notes: He is quoting our משנה, which says a vow comparing food to נותר or פיגול makes the food forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer רמי בר חמא's question from step 11 using the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a person comparing food to שלמים meat links to the meat's original forbidden status or to its current permitted status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that a vow comparing food to נותר or פיגול takes effect.
